newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply higher led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply higher led by gold.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply higher Thursday, led by heavy short covering in gold which pushed the April gold contract back up to its highest level in nearly a month.

"There's been some good liquidation of short positions going on all week in gold, and the shortcovering accelerated today once the downtrend line going back a couple of months was broken above this week's highs," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.

COMEX April gold ended up $5.00 an ounce, after seeing its highest levels intraday since January 29 at $354.00. The April/June spread continued to narrow, ending at $1.90 an ounce. Estimated total futures volume was a high 60,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $350.40/90 an ounce compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $345.00 and the New York close Wednesday at $345.00/50.

Traders said sentiment was also helped by news that the South African Reserve Bank governor, Chris Stals, said he thought the Belgian and Dutch central bank gold sales last year would not be followed by other central bank gold sales.
Gold prices saw three year lows last week, partly fuelled by fears of further European central bank gold sales.
But funds had been covering short positions for several days, analysts said, with COMEX gold interest Wednesday at 192,448 contracts, down 7,270 lots since last Thursday.
Implied lease rates had also fallen sharply this week, to around 1.30 percent for the one month rate from over 2.0 pct earlier this month, suggesting shorts were unwinding positions.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's gold and silver stocks index ended up 3.76 points at 118.70 Thursday, its highest level since late December.
Gold was stronger than silver Thursday, with the spot gold/silver ratio ending at 66.9, up from 66.7 Wednesday, and a 21 month low at 65.6 on February 14.
COMEX March silver ended up 4.0 cents at $5.23 an ounce, after seeing an intraday high at $5.260, its highest level.
Until Thursday, silver has helped to lead the recovery in gold with spot silver seeing a six month high last week.

In silver market news, Goldfields Mineral Services (GFMS) said Thursday that a surge in Indian silver demand during the second half of 1996 led to a further drawdown in above-ground world silver stocks.
Gold was stronger than platinum also Thursday, as some platinum/gold spreads were unwound, traders said.
The April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread ended at $19.30 an ounce, down from $21.60 Thursday, and off its contract high at $26.60 seen last week.
NYMEX April platinum closed up $2.70 at $371.90 an ounce, while NYMEX March palladium ended up just five cents at $135.50.

But the physical palladium market remained tight also, after spot prices saw a nine month high last week, reflecting ongoing supply problems due to the breakdown of the Russian/Japanese contract talks, traders said.
Russia is the world's largest producer of palladium.
But hedge fund activity may also be behind palladium's price rise, analysts noted.
The February issue of "Insitutional Investor" magazine, published this week, said hedge fund Tiger Management, run by Julian Robertson, had been buying "tons of palladium" recently.
"At some point - I don't know when - all these people are going to be asking, 'where are we going to get our palladium'," the magazine quoted Robertson saying.
"And the only place will be us," he said.
Tiger Management has about $8 billion under management.
